faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.sub: Everything you need to know before starting your French journey.
faq.q1: How can I prepare for TEF Canada online?
faq.a1: We offer personalized 1-on-1 sessions with certified native French teachers, full mock TEF Canada exams, AI-powered speaking simulation for the Expression Orale, and detailed examiner-style feedback for all four skills.
faq.q2: What is the difference between TEF and TCF?
faq.a2: TEF (Test d'Évaluation de Français) and TCF (Test de Connaissance du Français) are both official French proficiency exams. TEF Canada and TCF Canada are accepted by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) for Express Entry and citizenship. Choose based on your immigration program and test availability. We help you decide during your free demo.
faq.q3: Are your French teachers native speakers?
faq.a3: Yes. Every teacher on our platform is a certified native French speaker with several years of teaching experience and specialized training for TEF, TCF, DELF and DALF exam preparation.
faq.q4: Can I book a free demo lesson?
faq.a4: Yes, we offer a 100% free, no-commitment discovery session where we assess your level, discuss your goals and exam timeline, and pair you with the right teacher.
faq.q5: What CLB score do I need for Canadian Express Entry?
faq.a5: Most Express Entry programs require at least CLB 7 in all four skills (Speaking, Listening, Reading, Writing). For maximum points under the French-language bonus, aim for CLB 7 or higher. Many of our students reach CLB 9 in speaking.
faq.q6: How long does it take to prepare for the TEF Canada exam?
faq.a6: Preparation time varies by starting level. Most students reach CLB 7 within 3 to 6 months of consistent training (3–4 sessions per week). Higher targets like CLB 9 may take 6 to 12 months. We provide a personalized roadmap after your free demo.
